proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter tradeoffs (e.g., I->H vs H outflow) and unstable peak height/width.
proposals.rationale: Aligns observation directly to the hospitalization-rate target via an explicit H compartment; adds only one extra state beyond SEIR to capture admission dynamics without relying on delay tuning. Suitable for high peakiness where a dedicated H state can absorb sharp admission pulses.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Fractional order can over-smooth or distort timing, potentially underestimating peak amplitude or shifting peak week if memory effects dominate.
proposals.rationale: Same target-aligned H observation, with fractional dynamics as a parsimonious way to add memory/heavy-tail effects that can stabilize sharp peaks and high-rate scaling without introducing additional compartments.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay can introduce sensitivity in peak timing; if true lag is near 0, a 1-week delay may systematically shift forecasts late.
proposals.rationale: Keeps explicit hospitalization state while allowing a minimal 1-week reporting/aggregation lag consistent with surveillance semantics; avoids the brittleness seen at longer delays and remains closely aligned to the target.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Compounded flexibility (fractional + delay) may create identifiability issues, yielding similar fits with different implied dynamics and unstable extrapolation near the peak.
proposals.rationale: Combines explicit H targeting with a minimal lag and fractional smoothing to reduce rolling-split instability under high peakiness while staying within a simple template family.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Observation mismatch to hospitalization-rate target can persist (I proxy not proportional to admissions), leading to biased amplitude and poorer peak calibration versus H-observed SEIHR.
proposals.rationale: Retains the previously best-performing baseline as a comparator while using the least brittle delay choice (1 week) suggested by prior sensitivity; included sparingly as a non-H fallback template.
